notes:
Company profile: RelayPulse Assistworks is a CCaaS provider (mid-market) focused on automated triage and agent-assist workflows for telco and retail verticals. Core product plugs into Zendesk and Genesys. They run multi-tenant SaaS for ~250 enterprise customers; typical concurrency pattern: large daytime spikes tied to marketing/incident events.

Business drivers: cost-sensitive high-volume chat deflection to reduce live-agent load; measurable unit economics required to push customers to automation. Interested in replacing an expensive OpenAI-based fallback and an in-house lightweight model that lacks reliability at scale.

POC goals / success metrics: achieve >=60% deflection rate for top-10 intents, maintain p95 latency <=250ms for agent-assist flows, and demonstrate per-conversation cost < $0.03 (goal) or token cost < $0.0008. Show quantized model with <2% quality regression on key intents.

Workload details: primarily short chat turns (avg 8-14 tokens per turn; avg convo length 10-15 turns). Monthly volume: ~40M messages; peak concurrent chats target for design: 6k-8k. Typical usage pattern: many short requests where batching/prefix KV caching can materially reduce token compute.

Technical preferences and constraints: prefer open/quantizable models (13B-class or distilled 7B for burst handling). Want model pinning and automated fallback to a smaller quantized variant during spikes. Must support tool-calling to create/update tickets (Zendesk API) and emit structured fields for routing to agents. Seeking autoscaling/dedicated pool option for predictable throughput.

Security/compliance: SOC2 required (in contract), SSO/SAML, audit logging and KMS encryption for customer data, at-rest encryption, and data residency controls for EU customers. Legal asks for 12-month retention controls and export controls checklist.

Risks called out by customer: potential quality loss from aggressive 4-bit quantization; unknowns around end-to-end latency when combining batching + tool-calls; cost/throughput tradeoffs during large bursts (marketing-driven spikes).

Quotes / call notes: "We need predictable unit economics — if the math doesn't hold, we can't flip more customers to automation," — Aaron Patel (CTO).
"Can't accept more than ~1-2% decrease in intent-classification accuracy after quantization, otherwise agent handoffs spike," — Lina Morales (Head of Product).

Integration / ops: primary integration points: Zendesk, Genesys, SSO provider (Okta), and internal observability (Datadog). Wants per-route token/latency billing visibility and a rollout plan (canary + automatic fallback).

Previous vendor experiments: tested OpenAI (good quality, poor unit economics), in-house distilled LLM (cheap but brittle under prefix reuse), vendorX (failed to meet latency at scale).

Next steps (short): 1) Redwood to deliver detailed cost model (batching + cache assumptions) and latency runbook by 2026-03-12. 2) Security to review SOC2 artifacts; legal to confirm data residency language. 3) POC: 2-week workload on dedicated pool focused on top-10 intents (kickoff 2026-03-15).

Stakes: mid-market expansion — if successful, RelayPulse will convert several large customers from manual routing to automated deflection and commit to dedicated capacity (estimated ARR $150k-$400k).

Contacts / champions: Aaron Patel (CTO), Lina Morales (Head of Product), Emily Zhou (Procurement). SE lead: Daniel Ortiz (Redwood). AE owner: Maya Chen.

Open items: security questionnaire follow-up (SEC-4472), detailed quantization perf/quality report, final POC budget approval.
